## Motivation

[FlashInfer #5021](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5021) (0.7.0) adds indexed, floor-aligned checkpoints to CuTe DSL KDA prefill, which SGLang needs for radix prefix caching.

## Modifications

- Opt-in `--linear-attn-prefill-backend flashinfer` for BF16, 128-dim safe-gate KDA on SM100/SM103.
- Map FlashInfer checkpoints to radix-cache track rows (FP32 state pools, padded gate/beta); write only radix-tracked checkpoints.
- KDA models pass raw beta logits in every phase. Kernel adapters own activation, without backend-dependent model flags or model mutation during backend construction. FlashInfer tensor validation runs during warmup.
- Call `flashinfer.kda.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cute-dsl")` directly. FlashInfer owns scheduling and workspace allocation; SGLang maps radix-cache checkpoint destinations once per tracked batch. Invalid scheduler/checkpoint metadata raises an assertion.
- Reject incompatible checkpoint intervals, TBO, and full prefill CUDA graphs at setup. FlashInfer validates safe gates during warmup. BCG keeps linear attention eager; verify uses its separately configured backend.
- Retain Triton fallback for a packed prefill containing only one token, which FlashInfer's current packed-prefill API excludes.

This PR leaves dependency pins unchanged; the current tree already pins FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1.

## Accuracy Tests

Historical default-selection experiment (reverted by `c0d8467478`; FlashInfer remains opt-in): pre-commit passed. The [registered CPU rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37808499136) passed all 10 tests on `a231d574ae`, after correcting the policy fixture to publish a resolved CUDA graph config. The [B200 rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37715933478) passed FlashInfer KDA kernel tests and GLM-5.3-Flash low-latency GSM8K on `70b968ef19`: score 0.932 over 500 questions. The server log confirms `decode=triton, prefill=flashinfer, verify=nv_cutedsl`. The follow-up commit changes only the unit fixture.

Previously reported on 8xGB300, FlashInfer 0.7.0: the original five KDA prefill cases, existing KDA decode/verify (11), and CuTe DSL KDA + GDN checkpoint smoke (2) passed.

The current GPU test file contains six checkpoint/layout cases and two numerical backend cases (tracked prefill and single-token fallback). The direct-call cleanup passes pre-commit and focused CPU checks: eight checked-in test methods, 22 raw-beta contract checks, six checkpoint harness cases exercising the production adapter with a substituted numerical kernel, and six metadata-hook cases. GPU imports and numerical kernels were isolated for these local CPU checks. The eight GPU cases passed on pre-rebase head `ae9847e073` on B300 (SM103), FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 and CUDA 13.0, in 207.87 seconds. The exact rebased-head rerun is reported below.

### Exact rebased-head GLM-5.3-Flash checks

Reran both prefix-cache methods on the **exact rebased head `706048f3fd`** (before the default-selection change), with the full upstream fix and no diagnostic patch: real `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` weights (revision `eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a`), **4xB300 / TP4**, BF16 KV and SSM caches, TileLang DSA, Triton decode, 16K prefill chunks, eager execution, and `--mamba-track-interval 256`. FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1 (Python TreeCore), Transformers 5.17.0. Both arms use `SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0` to compile the exercised GEMM shapes on demand; the initial exhaustive startup compilation was stopped before probe requests.

**Kernel/configuration checks:** 23 tests passed, including all eight FlashInfer KDA numerical/layout cases, in 229.46 seconds. Pre-commit and focused CPU contract/metadata checks also passed.

**Cold versus cached continuation:** score the same fixed 167-token continuation after 32,769 / 36K / 72K context tokens. All target scores are finite; inputs are identical between backends.

| KDA prefill | Context | Cold/cached absolute logprob difference mean / p90 / max | Warm/repeat mean | Cached tokens warm / repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| triton | 32769 | 0.022187 / 0.000521 / 2.914499 | 0.017015 | 32768 / 32768 |
| triton | 36000 | 0.006804 / 0.000954 / 0.562500 | 0.003408 | 35840 / 35840 |
| triton | 72000 | 0.005175 / 0.000746 / 0.500000 | 0.003549 | 71936 / 71936 |
| flashinfer | 32769 | 0.009283 / 0.000480 / 1.046875 | 0.003289 | 32768 / 32768 |
| flashinfer | 36000 | 0.003019 / 0.000722 / 0.312500 | 0.003292 | 35840 / 35840 |
| flashinfer | 72000 | 0.003710 / 0.000662 / 0.346874 | 0.002871 | 71936 / 71936 |

**Branching corruption check from #42178:** cache an 8,320-token prefix; score copying a 167-token span from branch A before and after an unrelated branch B extends the shared prefix. Three different spans/seeds per backend.

| KDA prefill | Copy mean logprob before | After competing request | Second request cache hit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| triton | -0.015645 | -0.016829 | 8192 |
| flashinfer | -0.015597 | -0.016357 | 8192 |

The pre-rebase controls dropped from approximately -0.02 to -1.35 after the competing request. The rebased runs retain high copy scores with both KDA prefill backends and resume at 8,192, keeping the pooled index group private. This reproducer no longer shows the large branching collapse.

Warm repeats and the aligned-boundary control are **not bit-exact** on GLM. The Triton aligned control has a 2.9145 maximum cold/cached difference and a 2.0505 maximum warm/repeat difference despite a small p90; these outliers preclude claiming exact cache parity. These measurements do not isolate the residual drift to a specific operator. HiCache host restore and current-head speed were not tested.

### GLM-5.3-Flash checks before rebase

2026-10-07, head `ae9847e073`, real GLM-5.3-Flash weights, 4xB300 TP4, BF16 KV/SSM caches, TileLang DSA, 16K prefill chunks, eager execution, Triton decode. FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1 (Python TreeCore), Transformers 5.17.0. Model revision `eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a`.

Cold versus cached scoring uses identical contexts and a fixed 167-token continuation. Values are absolute logprob difference mean / p90 / max.

| Layout / prefill | 36K | 72K |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| PR head, Triton | 0.0044 / 0.0006 / 0.312 | 0.0023 / 0.0004 / 0.178 |
| PR head, FlashInfer | 0.0081 / 0.0009 / 0.550 | 0.0043 / 0.0007 / 0.344 |
| Device fix, Triton | 0.0089 / 0.0004 / 0.595 | 0.0040 / 0.0008 / 0.314 |
| Device fix, FlashInfer | 0.0045 / 0.0007 / 0.312 | 0.0054 / 0.0005 / 0.500 |

The branching check warms a prefix ending inside a 256-token index group, scores copying a span from the first suffix, then rescoring follows a competing request with unrelated text. Values below average three different 167-token copy spans.

| Layout / prefill | Copy mean logprob before | After competing request | Second request cache hit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PR head, Triton | -0.0189 | -1.3455 | 8320 |
| PR head, FlashInfer | -0.0169 | -1.3452 | 8320 |
| Device fix, Triton | -0.0158 | -0.0147 | 8192 |
| Device fix, FlashInfer | -0.0145 | -0.0159 | 8192 |

Before rebase, head `ae9847e073` lacked #42178. Both backends reproduced its pooled-index branching corruption; the device-cache portion of that fix, ported only into the isolated test checkout, removed the collapse. The PR has now been rebased onto main `7760d5264a`, which contains the full merged #42178 fix. The earlier diagnostic measurements below retain their original source provenance.

Warm repeats and the 32,768-token aligned-resume control are not bit-exact on GLM; residual small drift is not isolated to KDA. At 72K on the old layout, warm/repeat cache depths also differ (65,536 / 71,936). Fixed-layout arms use the required 256-token decode tracking interval; old-layout arms use 64. Probe requests generate zero tokens, and prefill tracking follows page/chunk geometry. HiCache host restore and latest-head speed were not tested.

### Historical Kimi K3 measurements

The following Kimi K3 results predate the current direct-call cleanup.

Kimi K3 real weights, 8xGB300, BF16 KV, DSpark: cold vs prefix-cache-resume logprobs over a fixed 167-token continuation (|Δlogprob| mean / p90 / max). Warm vs warm is bit-exact in all cases.

| Config | 36k ctx | 72k ctx |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DCP8, Triton prefill | 0.044 / 0.149 / 0.69 | 0.050 / 0.174 / 1.04 |
| DCP8, FlashInfer prefill | 0.043 / 0.147 / 0.55 | 0.055 / 0.215 / 0.61 |
| TP8, Triton prefill | 0.051 / 0.190 / 0.69 | 0.059 / 0.213 / 0.86 |

FlashInfer matches Triton. The drift is from chunk layout, not state restore: a resume on a cold chunk boundary (32768) is bit-exact.

## Speed Tests

These are historical measurements from the wrapper-based integration. The current direct API can read packed sequence offsets on the host to size its workspace and allocates that workspace within each call; performance and D2H behavior need remeasurement on the latest head.

Kimi K3 NVFP4 dummy weights, 8xGB300 TP8/DCP8, bs1, 131k in / 1k out, 95% prefix hit, A/B/A x10:

| Metric | Triton | FlashInfer |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Normal TTFT, median | 0.429 s | 0.411 s |
| Output throughput, median | 406.5 tok/s | 407.4 tok/s |
| KDA GPU time per layer (EXTEND trace) | 421 µs | 219 µs |
| KDA-associated D2H copies | 0 | 0 |

An intermittent ~6.7 s TTFT stall appears with both backends and is not attributed to KDA.

Kernel-only KDA prefill (checkpoints off), K3 shape on one TP8 rank (12 heads x 128), single GB300, bf16 in / fp32 state, median of 5 (ms). Backends that fall back to Triton at these lengths are omitted: `nvidia_kda` (needs >1 sequence), `flashkda` (caps at 2048 tokens/seq).

| Case | Triton | FlashInfer | ptx_kda | cutedsl |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16k | 1.18 | 0.87 | 0.72 | 1.51 |
| 32k | 2.09 | 1.37 | 1.13 | 2.67 |
| 64k | 3.95 | 2.38 | 1.94 | 4.94 |
| 128k, one sequence | 7.76 | 4.36 | 3.65 | 9.61 |
| 128k as 8x16k chunks | 3.82 | 1.18 | 2.66 | 7.52 |

FlashInfer is 1.3-1.8x Triton on a single sequence and 3.2x on the 8x16k shape chunked prefill actually issues, where it batches the sequences into one kernel. `ptx_kda` is ~20% faster on a single sequence but 2.3x slower on that chunked shape; it is also not measured here with checkpoints on, which its own fallback note says routes tracked batches to Triton. `cutedsl` cannot serve K3 at all (no safe gate, no interior checkpoints).

## Checklist

- [x] Format and code style checks
- [x] Add registered tests
- [x] Kernel-level accuracy and speed results
- [ ] Full Kimi K3 output parity with real weights

The initial MMMU attempts failed before evaluation because `sgl-eval` was missing and then dataset metadata targeted the shared read-only HF cache. The final runs above use the pinned evaluator and a writable local cache. The custom acceptance probe was discarded; the reported comparison comes from the existing registered sgl-eval test.

Both arms use `SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0` to compile the exercised GEMM shapes on demand; the initial exhaustive startup compilation was stopped before probe requests.

**Kernel/configuration checks:** 23 tests passed, including all eight FlashInfer KDA numerical/layout cases, in 229.46 seconds. Pre-commit and focused CPU contract/metadata checks also passed.
